name: sportsci-figures
description: Publication-grade figures, three-line tables and a Results document (.docx / .md) for sport, exercise, health and psychology studies, in an all-Chinese or all-English set with one navy palette. Runs the analysis from a design spec for RCT pre-post (ANCOVA), crossover and multi-timepoint (mixed models), single-group pre-post / repeated measures, questionnaire surveys (reliability, EFA, regression, bootstrap mediation, moderation) and meta-analysis, and offers figure blocks for 26 more data types (CGM, EMG, force, SPM, survival, ROC, omics, GPS). Also checks raw data files and writes a methods explanation. Use for 数据分析, 结果, 作图, 图表, 三线表, 问卷信效度, 中介/调节, 前后测, 学位论文结果章, or any results figure/table request. Does not polish or write prose (use sportsci-writing), choose a topic (use sportsci-topic) or manage citations (use sportsci-refs).
---

# sportsci-figures

Figures, tables and the Results section, done the same way every time: one style, two language sets (`zh` all-Chinese, `en`
all-English), numbers that always come from code. **Follow this file; do not improvise a style.**

Three ways in — pick by what the user has:

| The user has … | Path | Section |
|---|---|---|
| a raw data file (Excel / CSV), design unclear | `python cli.py intake data.xlsx -o intake` → de-identified data, data-quality report, draft `design.json` | §2 |
| a standard design (RCT, crossover, multi-time, single group, questionnaire, meta-analysis) | write / edit `design.json`, `python cli.py results` | §2 |
| any other data shape (waveforms, survival, ROC, omics, tracking …) | compose figure blocks from `pubstyle.figures` | §3 |

---

## First use (once)

The commands in this skill come from a Python package that ships in this folder. Before the first command, check it is installed:

```bash
sportsci-figures --help
```

If the shell says the command is not found, install it from this skill's folder (Python 3.10+):

```bash
python -m pip install -e <path to this skill folder>
```

If the package is installed but the command is still not found (common on Windows, where pip puts scripts in a folder that is not on PATH), use `python -m sportsci_figures.cli <command>` instead: it is the same program. From a source checkout, `python cli.py <command>` in this folder also works. Do this check once per machine, not before every command.

## 0. Ten-line summary

1. Decide the language set once (`zh` or `en`). Never mix languages in one deliverable.
2. `from sportsci_figures.pubstyle import apply_style, save_figure, ResultsDoc, figures as pf`, then **`apply_style(lang)` before any figure**.
3. Standard designs: write a `design.json` and run `python cli.py results` — never hand-code those analyses.
4. Other data: compose figures from `pf` blocks (§3). No `plt.style.use`, seaborn themes, or matplotlib default colours.
5. Every panel: bold lowercase letter + short title (`panel_title(ax, "a", "Change from baseline")`); no overall figure title.
6. Show **individual data** when n < ~60 plus a **model estimate with 95% CI**; effect sizes and exact P in the figure/table, never stars.
7. Colours are roles: intervention = navy `#112378`, control = sand `#C9A66B` (dashed lines), contrast/harm = terracotta `#C4573F`; doses = `dose_colors(n)`.
8. `save_figure(fig, stem)` → 300-dpi PNG + vector PDF, stamped "Simulated data" unless `simulated=False` (real data only).
9. Tables are three-line (`ResultsDoc.table`); numbers in text come from analysis objects, wording ("differed" / "did not differ") is chosen by code from P / CI.
10. **Open every PNG you produce** and run the checklist in §7. English figures must contain zero Chinese characters (`save_figure` raises).

---

## 1. Language set

| Signal | Set |
|---|---|
| Chinese request, 中文论文 / 开题 / 学位论文 / 国内期刊 | `zh` |
| English request, SCI journal, international submission | `en` |
| both | run twice (`-l both` or `for lang in ("zh", "en")`) → `…/zh/`, `…/en/` |
| unclear | ask once; default to the language of the request |

Layout, colours, sizes and statistics are identical in both sets. Differences: labels and captions (`图 1  标题` below / `Figure 1. Title`),
fonts (Arial + CJK fallback; docx 宋体/黑体 vs Times New Roman), minus sign (`-` in zh, `−` in en), footer tag. Use `tr("中文", "English")` for every
label so one script produces both sets. Full text: `reference/STYLE_SPEC_ZH.md`, `reference/STYLE_SPEC_EN.md`.

---

## 2. Standard designs: `design.json` → Results package

```bash
python cli.py intake data.xlsx -o intake                         # optional: raw file -> data_clean.csv, intake_report.md, design_draft.json
python cli.py new-design -t survey -o design.json                # parallel_prepost | crossover | multitime | meta | single_group | survey
python cli.py check-design design.json -d data.csv               # spec valid + data run through the analysis
python cli.py results design.json -d data.csv -o results -l both # add --chapter 4 for degree-thesis numbering (图 4-1 / Figure 4.1)
python cli.py results design.json --simulate -o rehearsal        # no data yet: rehearse with the spec's "simulate" block (tagged simulated)
```

Output per language: `figures/*.png|pdf`, `tables.xlsx`, `results.docx`, `results.md`, `methods_explained.md` (each analytic choice explained
with this study's numbers), plus `analysis.json` (every estimate) and `design_used.json`. Text, tables and figures come from the same objects,
so they cannot disagree.

| Study | `design` | Engine reports |
|---|---|---|
| parallel groups, baseline + follow-up | `parallel_prepost` | ANCOVA (baseline covariate), change scores, Hedges g, estimation panel |
| every participant in every condition | `crossover` | random-intercept LMM, EMMs, contrasts (Holm), dose trend, d_z |
| parallel groups, ≥ 3 visits | `multitime` | constrained longitudinal LMM + supplementary group × time mixed ANOVA (GG-corrected) |
| one group, 2+ visits | `single_group` | paired t + Wilcoxon / RM-ANOVA (Mauchly, Greenhouse–Geisser, Bonferroni pairwise); states the no-control limitation |
| questionnaire | `survey` | α, item–total r, KMO/Bartlett, EFA (PAF + varimax), Harman, correlations, group differences (BH q), regression (B, β, VIF), bootstrap mediation, moderation |
| pooling studies | `meta` | DerSimonian–Laird + Hartung–Knapp, subgroups, leave-one-out, Egger (k ≥ 10), meta-regression |

Multiplicity: primary outcome Holm, secondary outcomes Benjamini–Hochberg within category; significance wording follows the adjusted P.
Spec fields and data layouts: `reference/DESIGN_SPEC.md`. From research question to spec: `reference/GAP_TO_DESIGN.md`.
`intake` only *guesses* the design, control group, primary outcome and reverse-keyed items — confirm every "open question" before `results`.

---

## 3. Any other data: pick the block by the *shape* of the data

| Data shape | Block (`pf.<name>`) |
|---|---|
| curve per participant (time, cycle, distance) | `ax_bands`, `ax_diff_band`, `ax_spm` |
| 1 number per participant, paired conditions | `ax_paired_estimate` |
| 1 number per participant, groups / ≥ 3 conditions | `ax_raincloud` |
| ≥ 3 time points by group | `ax_multitime(..., band=True)`, `ax_timepoints` |
| pre/post by arm | `ax_prepost` |
| many outcomes | `fig_forest_effects` |
| agreement / reliability | `ax_identity`, `ax_bland_altman` |
| ordinal items / scales | `ax_likert`, `ax_corr_heatmap`, `ax_radar`, `ax_mediation` |
| time-to-event | `km_estimate`, `ax_km`, `at_risk_table` |
| binary prediction | `ax_roc`, `ax_calibration` |
| evidence synthesis | `fig_meta_forest`, `ax_funnel` |
| dose–response | `ax_dose_response`, `fit_band` + `ax_fit_band` |
| individual response | `ax_waterfall` |
| composition | `ax_stacked_bars` |
| omics | `ax_volcano`, `ax_heatmap`, `ax_ellipse` |
| spatial | `ax_ellipse`, `ax_pitch_heat` |
| eye tracking (fixations on a stimulus) | `ax_gaze_heatmap`, `fig_gaze_heatmap_grid`, `gaze_density`, `to_screen_px` (see *Eye tracking* below) |
| design / flow | `draw_flow`, `ax_gantt` |

All 26 data types have a runnable example in `examples/gallery/` (pictures in `assets/pubstyle_gallery/`); selection rules and colour
conventions in `reference/DATA_TYPE_GUIDE.md`; signatures in `reference/API.md`; scenario → picture in `reference/FIGURE_CATALOG.md`.
If no block fits, plain matplotlib after `apply_style` still uses the navy palette (default colour cycle and colour map are set) — but add
panel titles, direct labels and CIs by hand to match §5.

```python
from sportsci_figures.pubstyle import apply_style, save_figure, condition_colors, panel_title, DOUBLE, ResultsDoc, figures as pf
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

apply_style("en")                                          # or "zh" — BEFORE any figure
col = condition_colors(["CON", "RT20", "RT30", "RT45"])    # CON sand; doses light periwinkle -> navy
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(DOUBLE, 3.4))
pf.ax_bands(ax, x, {"CON": (mu0, se0), "RT20": (mu1, se1)}, col, dashed=["CON"])
ax.set_xlabel("Time after start (h)"); ax.set_ylabel("Glucose (mmol/L)")
panel_title(ax, "a", "Glucose time course")
save_figure(fig, "out/fig2_timecourse")                    # -> .png (300 dpi) + .pdf, tagged "Simulated data"

d = ResultsDoc("en")                                       # profile="thesis", chapter=4 for 小四 / 1.5 spacing / Figure 4.1
d.title("3  Results"); d.notice()                          # notice() only when data are simulated
d.para(f"{n} participants were included …")                # numbers from variables, never typed
d.figure("out/fig2_timecourse.png", "Glucose time course. a, …")
d.table(df, "Baseline characteristics", note="Mean ± SD …")
d.save("out/results.docx")
```
Complete two-language reference script: `examples/pubstyle_demo.py`.

### Eye tracking: one input contract, one look

Fixation heat maps look the same for every user and every data set because nothing in them is estimated from the data or left to taste.

| Fixed by the function | Set by you (state it once) |
|---|---|
| Gaussian kernel of fixed width `sigma = 0.02` of the screen width (about 1°), not data-driven | `screen=(W, H)` of the display, in pixels |
| Value = density **relative to an even spread** (1 = even): independent of resolution, fixation count and the unit of the weights | `units`: `"px"` or `"norm"` (0-1) |
| One colour map (`GAZE_CMAP`), alpha 0.45, scale 0 to the 99th percentile of the panel | `origin`: `"topleft"` (EyeLink, SMI, Tobii px), `"bottomleft"`, `"center"` (PsychoPy pix) |
| Equal weight per participant when `participant=` is given | `weights` (durations), `participant` (ids), `stimulus_box` for an image smaller than the screen |

Rules: pass `participant` for every group map (otherwise one long viewer dominates); use `n_text="auto"` so the counts come from the data;
a panel with fewer than 3 usable fixations says so instead of drawing a blank scale; a warning means more than 5 % of fixations fall off the
screen, so check `screen` / `units` / `origin` before trusting the picture. Colour bars are per panel by default; use
`fig_gaze_heatmap_grid(..., shared_scale=True)` when colours must be compared between panels. A heat map is descriptive: report AOI
statistics (dwell time, first fixation) in a table for any claim.

---

## 4. Hard rules

**Integrity.** Every number in a figure, table or sentence is computed from the data. Simulated data: `ResultsDoc.notice()` plus the footer
tag on every figure, and say so in Methods. Conceptual drawings say "conceptual schematic (not data)". Never write "significant" for P ≥ 0.05;
never write "equivalent" for a non-significant difference; label unadjusted secondary analyses exploratory.

**Figure anatomy.** Width 7.2 in (two columns) or 3.5 in (one); compound heights 2.7–5.3 in. Fonts 7 pt, ticks 6.5 pt, annotations 5.5–6 pt,
panel letters 9 pt bold, nothing below 5 pt. No top/right spines; the only grid is faint dotted horizontal hairlines (`hair_y`). Axis label =
quantity + unit (`Glucose (mmol/L)`); time axes say what t = 0 is. Legends frameless, direct labels preferred. Say whether bands are SEM or 95% CI.

**Colours (fixed roles, `pubstyle/style.py`).** primary navy `#112378` · control sand `#C9A66B` · contrast terracotta `#C4573F` · middle dose
`#3F4F9E` · slate `#8E98C6` · teal `#2F6F73` · ink `#161A26` · annotation grey `#626778`. Diverging maps terracotta–paper–navy (`DIVERGING`),
sequential paper→navy (`SEQ`). Never rainbow maps, pure red/green/blue, `viridis`/`magma`, or other palettes —
with **one named exception**: eye-tracking fixation heat maps use the rainbow-type `turbo` map, because that is the field's convention and
hot spots must read on photographs. It is the default of the gaze blocks only (`GAZE_CMAP`, overridable with `cmap=`); everything else, including
other heat maps drawn on a stimulus or a pitch, stays navy.

**Tables.** Three-line only (thick top and bottom rules, thin header rule, no vertical lines, no shading); first column left, others centred.
`mean ± SD`, `n (%)`, `estimate (95% CI)`, P as `<0.001` or three decimals (never `0.000`). Table 1 reports SMD, not only P. A footnote states
the model/test, adjustment, multiplicity rule and abbreviations. Export the same tables to Excel (`save_tables_xlsx`).

**Statistics (defaults).** Pre–post with control: ANCOVA on follow-up with baseline covariate, Hedges g. Crossover: LMM with participant random
intercept and period, EMMs, Holm-adjusted contrasts, d_z. Skewed outcomes: log-transform (ratios, mark `†`) or non-parametric. Report missing
data, exclusions and sensitivity analyses.

---

## 5. Finish rules (polished, not merely correct)

- CI bars and whiskers in the **group colour**, no caps, white-edged mean markers — never black error bars over coloured data.
- Time courses: mean line + **shaded 95% CI ribbon**, control dashed, **direct labels** at line ends (collision-free) instead of a legend.
- A single model contrast is an **estimation panel** (`results.plots.diff_estimate`: sampling distribution + estimate + CI + numbers), not a one-row forest.
- Densities taper smoothly (`ax_raincloud`); long tick labels wrap (`wrap_label`); panel widths follow content, `wspace` ≈ 0.35–0.45.
- Forest plots: category colour bars, zebra rows, value column next to the axis, "favours" labels on top.

Design rationale and the palette: `docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md`.

---

## 6. Workflow for an AI agent

1. Raw file? Run `intake` first and work on `data_clean.csv`; never copy the `_private/` ID map into outputs or prompts.
2. Identify design and outcomes by role (primary / secondary / safety); decide the language set (§1).
3. Standard design → `design.json` + `results`. Otherwise do the statistics with statsmodels / scipy / pingouin and keep tidy DataFrames.
4. Build figures with blocks, one script for both languages (`tr`). Save with `save_figure`; open each PNG; run §7.
5. Tables as DataFrames of strings (`fmt_msd`, `fmt_ci`, `fmt_p_table`) → `ResultsDoc.table` + `save_tables_xlsx`.
6. Results text with f-strings and conditional wording; number figures/tables in order of first mention; `ResultsDoc.save`.
7. Run `python -m pytest -q` after changing library code.
8. Report what was produced and where, the language set, exploratory/unadjusted analyses and limits (e.g. simulated data). Hand over
   `methods_explained.md`: whoever presents the work must be able to explain every analytic choice.

---

## 7. Self-check before handing over

Figures (open the PNG): language consistent (en has no Chinese) · no tofu boxes, minus and Greek render · nothing overlaps or is clipped ·
panel letters + titles aligned · units on every axis, t = 0 defined, n shown · raw data + estimate ± CI, band type stated · colours per §4,
control dashed, dose order readable in greyscale · "Simulated data" tag when applicable · PNG + PDF exist.
Tables: three-line, header bold, first column left · number formats per §4 · footnote with model, adjustment, multiplicity.
Text: every number traceable to a variable · conditional wording · exploratory analyses flagged · numbering follows first mention.

## 8. Known pitfalls

- `font.family` must stay a **list** (`['Arial', 'Microsoft YaHei']`) for per-character fallback; `apply_style` sets it — do not override rcParams afterwards.
- Figures created before `apply_style` keep the old fonts and colours.
- No CJK font installed → `has_cjk_font()` is False and zh figures show boxes: install Noto Sans CJK SC or Microsoft YaHei first.
- Windows console: set `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` to print Chinese.
- Survey scale names become columns and must not clash with existing column names; feed raw item answers (reverse items are recoded by the engine).

## 9. Files

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `sportsci_figures/pubstyle/` | style (`style.py`), figure blocks (`figures.py`, `figures_ext.py`), tables (`tables.py`), Word document (`report.py`) |
| `sportsci_figures/results/` | design-spec engine: `spec.py`, `analysis*.py`, `builders*.py`, `plots.py`, `explain.py`, `simulate.py`, `build.py` (`run_results`) |
| `sportsci_figures/intake.py`, `privacy.py`, `profiler.py` | raw-file check, de-identification, layout detection |
| `sportsci_figures/cli.py`, `cli.py` | command line |
| `config/design_templates/` | runnable templates for the six designs; `config/meta_extraction_template.csv` |
| `reference/` | `DESIGN_SPEC`, `GAP_TO_DESIGN`, `DATA_TYPE_GUIDE`, `FIGURE_CATALOG`, `API`, `STYLE_SPEC_ZH`, `STYLE_SPEC_EN` |
| `docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md` | design rationale, palette, finish rules |
| `examples/pubstyle_demo.py`, `examples/gallery/` | two-language reference script; 26 data types (`python examples/gallery/make_gallery.py`) |
| `assets/` | rendered gallery and examples — the look to match |
| `tests/` | estimates recover simulated truth, reference implementations agree, both languages end to end, palette guard |

name: sportsci-refs
description: Reference management for Word documents (theses, proposals, papers) with Zotero. Searches literature (Crossref, Europe PMC, OpenAlex), verifies DOIs against Crossref, parses a typed GB/T 7714 list to RIS / CSL-JSON, matches it to a Zotero collection, turns plain "[n]" citations into live Zotero citation fields, edits and renumbers a document that already has fields without breaking them, and machine-verifies the result. Use for 参考文献, 引文, Zotero, 引文域, GB/T 7714, 文献表, 引用编号乱了, 检查引文, DOI 核验, 让 Zotero 管理这篇的参考文献, or "make the citations in this docx refresh automatically".
---

# sportsci-refs

One pipeline from "a draft with typed `[n]` citations" to "citations Zotero can refresh, a self-consistent bibliography, and a document
that still opens". Every step has a command and a check; nothing here is "be careful".

## First use (once)

The commands in this skill come from a Python package that ships in this folder. Before the first command, check it is installed:

```bash
sportsci-refs --help
```

If the shell says the command is not found, install it from this skill's folder (Python 3.10+):

```bash
python -m pip install -e <path to this skill folder>
```

If the package is installed but the command is still not found (common on Windows, where pip puts scripts in a folder that is not on PATH), use `python -m sportsci_refs.cli <command>` instead: it is the same program. From a source checkout, `python cli.py <command>` in this folder also works. Do this check once per machine, not before every command.

## Iron rules

1. **Never invent.** Authors, years, volume/pages, DOIs: if it is missing, ask the author or read the paper. A candidate list is not a reference list.
2. **Fields first.** In a paragraph with citation fields, edit only runs outside fields. Never rewrite or delete a paragraph that holds field markers.
3. **Back up, write a NEW file, verify.** Every command writes a new file and refuses to overwrite the source. After any write run `verify`; every count must be 0.

## Pipeline

| # | Goal | Command | Check |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Is Zotero reachable? | `sportsci-refs status` | a 502 comes from a local proxy: Zotero is simply not running |
| 1 | Candidate literature | `sportsci-refs search "<keywords>" --n 15 --year-from 2015 -o candidates.md` | candidates only; the author reads and decides |
| 2 | Verify DOIs | `sportsci-refs check-doi list.txt -o doi.md` | `MISMATCH` = real DOI on the wrong paper; `EXISTS` = no title to compare; `NODOI` → check CNKI / Wanfang by hand |
| 3 | Typed list → Zotero | `sportsci-refs parse refs.txt -o refs` → import `refs.ris` in Zotero | entries the parser was unsure about are listed |
| 4 | List ↔ collection | `sportsci-refs match refs.txt -c "<collection>" -o zotero_match.json` | title matches below 0.97 go to manual review |
| 5 | `[n]` → live fields | `sportsci-refs fieldify thesis.docx -m zotero_match.json --superscript --dry-run`, then without `--dry-run` | split-run citations are reported, not touched |
| 6 | Word: style + Refresh | Zotero → Document Preferences → choose the required style → Refresh | rebuilds numbers, bibliography, tab characters |
| 7 | Edit text later | `sportsci-refs edit thesis.docx -r "old=>new" -o v2.docx` | only plain text outside fields changes |
| 8 | Numbers out of order | `sportsci-refs renumber v2.docx -o v3.docx`, then Word → Refresh | bibliography is reordered by Zotero, not by the tool |
| 9 | Verify before delivery | `sportsci-refs verify v3.docx -o report.md` and `sportsci-refs compare old.docx v3.docx` | all counts 0; only `word/document.xml` changed |
| – | No Zotero | `sportsci-refs format refs.ris` | GB/T 7714-2015 numeric list from CSL / RIS |
| – | Framed templates | `sportsci-refs frames thesis.pdf` | pages where the frame ends early |

Settings (Zotero user ID, data folder, e-mail) go in `config/local.toml` or environment variables — copy `config/local.example.toml`; never put
them in code or commit them. Full playbook with every pitfall: `reference/ZOTERO_PLAYBOOK.md`.

## What `verify` checks (all must be 0)

field markers balanced · payload JSON valid · citationID unique · display = payload · numbers = order of first appearance ·
citation before sentence-final punctuation · no two adjacent fields without text · bibliography numbered 1..N with a tab after each number ·
bibliography entry matches the cited title · cited-but-not-listed / listed-but-not-cited.
A freshly `fieldify`-ed file that Zotero has not refreshed yet will report missing tabs and title mismatches: expected until step 6.
**Checkers lie too**: en dash vs hyphen, `instrText` split over runs, RTF-encoded dashes in `formattedCitation`. Before reporting "N problems",
open the first one by hand.

## Python

```python
from sportsci_refs import parse_gbt_list, format_list, to_ris
from sportsci_refs.docx_fields import fieldify, verify
from sportsci_refs.fieldedit import FieldDoc

doc = FieldDoc("thesis_zotero.docx")
doc.replace("下降趋势", "降低趋势")                               # plain text only
i, grp = doc.citations()[0]
from sportsci_refs.fieldedit import detach
els = detach(grp)
ok, msg = doc.insert_before_anchor(j, "。", els)                # move a citation in front of the full stop; refuses ambiguous anchors
doc.refresh_numbers()
doc.save("thesis_v2.docx")                                      # refuses to overwrite, refuses to drop fields
```

## Pitfalls

- A Zotero field is 5+ runs; a 70-run paragraph often has only 25 plain-text runs. "Delete all runs and append one" silently destroys citations.
- Never serialise `document.xml` through a parser that moves inline namespace declarations (`xmlns:a` on pictures): Word reports a corrupt file.
  `fieldify` splices strings; `fieldedit` uses lxml which keeps declarations; all other package parts are copied byte for byte.
- Press Refresh only when the Zotero library is complete: missing items become `[?]` and numbering shifts. Sync before switching machines.
- Never write test items to a real library (the local API cannot delete: 501) and never touch `zotero.sqlite` directly; item IDs are read from a copy.
- Word re-saves change the package silently; re-check `docProps/custom.xml` (holds the Zotero style) and the field counts afterwards.
- A reference "verified" by DOI only exists with matching metadata; whether it supports the sentence is the author's job.

## Files

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `sportsci_refs/search.py`, `doi.py` | candidate search, DOI verification |
| `sportsci_refs/ris.py`, `gbt7714.py` | GB/T 7714 text ↔ CSL-JSON ↔ RIS; GB/T 7714-2015 formatter |
| `sportsci_refs/zotero.py`, `net.py`, `config.py` | local Zotero API (proxy-safe), item IDs from a database copy, settings |
| `sportsci_refs/docx_fields.py` | `fieldify`, `verify`, `compare_parts`, `field_diff`, `diagnose` |
| `sportsci_refs/fieldedit.py` | field-safe edits: replace, move, renumber (`FieldDoc`) |
| `sportsci_refs/pdf_frames.py` | page-by-page frame check |
| `reference/ZOTERO_PLAYBOOK.md` | full playbook (Chinese): environment, stages, pitfalls, delivery, framed templates |
| `tests/` | offline tests (no network, no running Zotero) |

Turns a vague interest into a defensible topic - a brief with Chinese and English search terms and real constraints, an evidence map from the student's own records (CNKI / PubMed / Zotero exports or sportsci-refs search) with overlap counts and nearest studies, a design chosen by an explicit rule table (parallel pre-post, crossover, multi-time, single group, survey, meta), exact sample size and the smallest effect the accessible n can detect, a green/yellow/red feasibility rubric with each rule printed, variant comparison, and a one-page topic card plus a design.json draft for sportsci-figures. # sportsci-topic

Counting and calculating, not brainstorming. A topic is acceptable when it is not already crowded, a design exists that can answer it,
the people and weeks are enough, and the instruments exist. Every one of those is a number or a rule here.

## First use (once)

The commands in this skill come from a Python package that ships in this folder. Before the first command, check it is installed:

```bash
sportsci-topic --help
```

If the shell says the command is not found, install it from this skill's folder (Python 3.10+):

```bash
python -m pip install -e <path to this skill folder>
```

If the package is installed but the command is still not found (common on Windows, where pip puts scripts in a folder that is not on PATH), use `python -m sportsci_topic.cli <command>` instead: it is the same program. From a source checkout, `python cli.py <command>` in this folder also works. Do this check once per machine, not before every command.

## Iron rules

1. **Never invent literature, effect sizes or "gaps".** Records come from files the student exports (or `sportsci-refs search`). A gap is a
   statement about the *record set* ("12 records cover P and I, none covers O"); say it that way. Whether it is a real gap is the author's judgement.
2. **The effect size needs a source** (paper DOI + table, pilot, or "smallest effect of interest"). No source = the sample size is only illustrative.
3. **Fix the primary outcome now.** Exactly one `primary = true`, before any data exist.
4. **Do not write the thesis.** The card ends with open items the author must do: read the nearest studies, write the one sentence on how the study differs.
5. **Every number comes from a command.** Never type a sample size, a count or a power into the answer from memory.

## What the agent does (and what the code does)

| Step | Who | How |
|---|---|---|
| Turn the idea into a brief: PICO + Chinese **and** English terms, outcomes with `needs`, constraints | agent + student | `sportsci-topic new` → fill `brief.toml` → `sportsci-topic check brief.toml` |
| Get records | student / `sportsci-refs` | export from CNKI / Wanfang / PubMed / Zotero (`.csv .ris .json .txt`), or `sportsci-refs search "<q>" -o c.md` and export; `--fetch` does it when sportsci-refs is installed |
| Evidence map | code | `sportsci-topic evidence brief.toml -r records.csv` |
| Design + sample size + feasibility + card | code | `sportsci-topic card brief.toml -r records.csv -o topic_out --lang zh` |
| Variants: change one axis, recount | code (agent proposes the alternatives) | add `[[variants.population]]` etc. to the brief → `sportsci-topic variants brief.toml -r records.csv` |
| Explain the card, name the next 3 actions | agent | read `topic_out/topic_card.md` and `topic_data.json`; do not add numbers that are not there |
| Hand over to analysis | code | `sportsci-figures check-design topic_out/design_draft.json` |

Search vocabulary is where the agent adds value: list synonyms, abbreviations, Chinese and English variants per facet. A thin vocabulary gives a falsely empty map.

## Commands

```bash
sportsci-topic new -o brief.toml                  # commented template
sportsci-topic check brief.toml                   # errors, warnings, design, the queries it would run
sportsci-topic evidence brief.toml -r cnki.csv -r pubmed.ris
sportsci-topic variants brief.toml -r cnki.csv [--two-axis]
sportsci-topic power two-sample -e 0.5            # n per group; add --dropout 0.15
sportsci-topic power two-sample --n 17            # smallest detectable d for 17 per group
sportsci-topic power ancova --delta 3 --sd 5 --r-prepost 0.6
sportsci-topic card brief.toml -r cnki.csv -o topic_out --lang zh   # topic_card.md + design_draft.json + topic_data.json
```

`power` tests: `two-sample` (d), `paired` (dz), `ancova`, `correlation` (r), `anova` (f, `--k`), `regression` (f², `--predictors`).

## How to read the card

- **Evidence map** — counts of records matching P+I, I+O, P+O, P+I+O, all years and last five. Fewer than 30 records = "a sketch": say so, ask for more records.
- **Overlap tier** — direct overlap in the last 5 years: 0 / 1–3 green, 4–9 yellow, ≥ 10 red. 1–3 neighbours is normal; the author must state the difference.
- **Sample size** — required n for the stated effect, power at the accessible n, and the smallest effect that n can detect (80 % power). If the accessible n can only
  detect d ≈ 1.0, the honest advice is a bigger effect (longer / stronger intervention), a within-subject design, or a different outcome — not a smaller n claim.
- **Variants** — a zero is only informative if the variant's own terms appear in the records; otherwise it is "not assessable".
- **Feasibility** — each row has its rule. Overall colour = the worst row. Do not average.

## Python

```python
from sportsci_topic.pipeline import run
r = run("brief.toml", ["cnki.csv", "pubmed.ris"], lang="zh")
r.assessment["overall"], r.evidence.direct_recent, r.plan.mdes_at_accessible, r.choice.design
open("topic_card.md", "w", encoding="utf-8").write(r.card)
```

## Pitfalls

- CNKI exports are often GBK/ANSI; the reader tries UTF-8 then GB18030. Headers like `Title-题名`, `Year-年`, `Summary-摘要` are recognised.
- A Chinese-only vocabulary matches nothing in PubMed records and vice versa — give both languages for every facet.
- `accessible_n` is people you can really enrol (before dropout). Do not enter the class size if only a third will volunteer.
- Multi-time-point mixed models have no closed-form power: the tool uses ANCOVA at the final time point (usually conservative) and says so.
- `ethics = "not_needed"` is a claim to confirm in writing with the department, not a default.
- The tool never says a topic is *good*; it says whether it is crowded, possible and affordable.

# Sport Science Writing & Polishing

A toolkit for producing genuinely human, journal-grade sport science writing in Chinese and English, with built-in statistics and Nature-style figure generation.

## Operating principles

Read these before doing anything else. They override any default writing instinct you may have.

### 1. Never fabricate

You may rephrase, restructure, translate, and tighten. You may **not**:
- invent numerical results, sample sizes, p-values, or effect sizes
- invent citations, DOIs, author names, or publication years
- infer a result that the data do not directly support
- change the direction of a finding to make it sound stronger

If a number, citation, or claim is missing, ask the user. Do not paper over the gap with plausible-sounding text.

### 2. The author's zero-tolerance list

The author of this skill reads three patterns as obvious AI traces and does not want them anywhere in running prose, in Chinese or in English. Published papers use them freely. This skill does not.

| 禁用 | 中文 | English | 改法 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 破折号 dashes | `——` `—` | `—`, spaced `–`, `--`, spaced ` - ` | 逗号、冒号，或拆成两句 |
| 分号 semicolons | `；` | `;` | 用句号切分 |
| 对照句 contrast frames | 不是……而是…… / 不只是（不仅是）……而是…… / 不是……，是…… / 并非……而是…… / 不再是……而是…… / 与其说……不如说…… / 不在于……而在于…… | not X but Y / It is not X, but Y, that … / not because X but because Y / not merely X but Y | 直接陈述 B。State Y directly. |

What stays allowed:

- **Semicolons inside brackets.** Grouped statistics such as `（t=2.10，P<0.05；t=2.45，P<0.05；t=2.3，P<0.05）` and citation lists such as `(refs 12; 15)` are standard. Even these should not pile up: more than one such bracket in a paragraph reads as generated.
- **Dashes in ranges and compounds.** `60–80%`, `weeks 1–4`, `muscle–bone unit` use an en-dash as a range or link mark.
- **Result statements with "but".** "The difference was not statistically significant but showed a trend (P = 0.06)" reports two findings. It is not a contrast frame.

Enumerated items get no exception. Write `1）…。2）…。` with full stops.

The same rules apply to your own replies and summaries to this user. `scripts/ai_trace_check.py` reports all three as hits marked "author rule".

### 3. Strip AI traces aggressively

The single most common failure mode of AI-written sport science is that it reads like AI. Reviewers and supervisors now spot it instantly. Before returning any polished text, mentally diff it against the AI-trace lists in `references/ai-traces-zh.md` and `references/ai-traces-en.md`, and study the concrete rewrite pairs in `references/before-after.md`. Those examples carry more information than any rule.

Removing traces is only half the job. Text with every AI word deleted can still read as generated, because it lacks what human authors add: specific anchors, evidence-calibrated hedging, field terms, and visible author judgment. For any English output (drafting, polishing, or zh→en translation), also read `references/human-voice-en.md` and rebuild paragraphs from their content instead of swapping words.

**Do not optimize for AI-detector evasion.**

Do not promise to bypass GPTZero, Turnitin, 知网 AIGC, PaperPass, or any other detector. If the user asks to "lower AI detection score", "pass AI detection", or similar, redirect the task to legitimate revision: make the prose more specific, evidence-grounded, field-appropriate, and author-like. Use `references/anti-detector.md` only as a cautionary note about why mechanical detector gaming hurts readability. Do not apply detector-evasion recipes as an objective.

Besides the zero-tolerance list, watch for:

- parenthetical asides "（...）" / "(...)" used to qualify claims → fold the qualifier into the sentence or drop it
- mechanical enumeration: 首先/其次/再者/最后, First/Second/Third/Finally → use natural prose flow
- "AI tell" vocabulary: delve, navigate, tapestry, landscape, realm, leverage, underscore, crucial, pivotal, robust, comprehensive, intricate, nuanced. 深入探讨, 全面分析, 至关重要, 具有重要意义, 值得注意的是, 综上所述
- stacked transitions: Moreover/Furthermore/Additionally back-to-back. 此外/另外/同时 连续出现
- name-and-restate paragraph shape (topic sentence → body → restate topic sentence)
- Chinese "的的不休" (3+ "的" within one clause) and "性/化/度" noun-stacking
- 对仗成癖: "不仅……而且……" / "既……又……" twice in one paragraph
- **对话残留与编辑痕迹**, the class that makes a manuscript read like a chat log. 第二人称（你/您/咱们）、指示读者（下面我们/请看/需要注意的是）、口语（其实/说白了/搞定/差不多）、第一人称叙事（我认为/本研究团队/笔者/本人）、角色词（课题组/我们组）、内部讨论话术（"或经导师复核后调整" / "待与导师商定"）、占位符（待补/TODO/XXX/上一版）、孤立的标点段。完整清单与改写见 `references/ai-traces-zh.md` 第七节。

Read the full reference lists for the replacement patterns. The goal is prose that a careful human author in this field would actually write, with nothing that is merely grammatical and feels generated.

### 4. Match the genre

Sport science writing has several registers. Decide first which genre you are in, then read the corresponding section of `references/article-structures.md`:

- SCI/SSCI empirical paper (IMRaD)
- Narrative review
- Systematic review / meta-analysis (PRISMA)
- Undergraduate / Master's / PhD thesis (Chinese or English)
- Conference abstract (structured, ~250 words)

Tone, hedge level, paragraph length, and section depth differ. A thesis Methods section is far more verbose than a journal Methods section. A narrative review has no separate Introduction section.

### 5. Match the field

Sport science spans physiology, biochemistry, biomechanics, motor control, sport psychology, training science, public health, and rehabilitation. Conventions differ:

- Physiology / biochemistry: VO2max, lactate, HR, hormones. Report mean ± SD, percent change, effect size (Cohen's d or Hedges' g)
- Psychology: scale scores, reliability (Cronbach's α), report 95% CI, prefer mixed-effects models for repeated measures
- Biomechanics: kinematic/kinetic variables, often n is small, report individual data alongside group means
- Training studies: pre/post designs, report ICC for reliability. Magnitude-based inference is now discouraged, so use standard NHST + ES
- Epidemiology / public health: OR, RR, HR (hazard ratio), adjust for confounders, report 95% CI

If the user does not specify the field, infer it from the variables they mention and confirm before drafting.

### 6. The tone stops defending, the content keeps everything

Remove self-undermining frames ("遗憾的是", "必须承认", "存在严重不足", "unfortunately", "we must acknowledge") and project-diary structure
("先……然后……最后", "first we… then we… finally we…"). Abstracts and introductions reach the question and the main result in their first
sentences. Conclusions do not end with new self-criticism. Details: `references/ai-traces-zh.md` §6.3–6.4, `references/ai-traces-en.md` §5.3–5.4,
`references/logic-check.md` §10–11.

This never extends to the content. The pre-specified primary outcome is reported whatever it shows and is never swapped for a better-looking
one. A null result is written as "未见差异 / did not differ" with P and the CI. The limitations paragraph stays, each limitation with its
consequence. A secondary or post-hoc result is never presented as the main finding.

### 7. A Word file has to look written by a person

Before any .docx leaves your hands (manuscript, submission copy, cover letter, supplement), run
`scripts/docx_finalize.py` and read `references/docx-delivery.md`. It fixes what generated documents give away:

- numbers: in Chinese text 4-digit numbers without separator (6045), 5+ digits with a comma (33,987), never a space
  inside a number. English paragraphs use commas from 1,000 up
- spaces: none between Chinese and Latin letters, digits or full-width punctuation, captions written "表1　表名",
  heading numbers followed by one full-width space, no double spaces
- layout: 宋体 + Times New Roman, title 小三 黑体, body 小四 with 1.5 line spacing, picture paragraphs single spacing,
  captions and tables 五号/小五, wide tables autofit. The target journal's own instructions override these defaults

Document metadata (author, created and modified times) is a personal setting. If `scripts/docx_metadata.local.py`
exists locally, the finalize script calls it. It is never committed.

Run `docx_finalize.py --check` and look at two or three rendered pages before saying the file is ready.

## Workflow

### When the user gives you raw text to polish

1. Read the text. Identify: language (zh / en / mixed), genre, field, target journal style if mentioned.
2. If the user asks for logic, rigor, argumentation, consistency, evidence alignment, or overclaiming checks, read `references/logic-check.md`. Audit the reasoning before polishing the prose.
3. Run a mental pass against the zero-tolerance list and the AI-trace checklist. If the text is heavily AI-generated, plan a deeper rewrite instead of word substitution. For English, follow the content-outward procedure in `references/human-voice-en.md` §0. If the source lacks the specifics a paragraph needs (sample, protocol, instrument, effect size), ask the user for them in a separate list instead of writing around the gap.
4. Polish in place. Preserve every verified number, citation, and factual claim verbatim. Do not preserve wording that overstates what the evidence supports.
5. If the text is in a file or can be saved to a temporary file, run `python scripts/ai_trace_check.py <file>` or `py scripts/ai_trace_check.py <file>` from the skill directory to catch missed formulaic patterns. Fix every HIT. Read each warn in context: it marks a pattern that is fine once but formulaic when repeated. The script only sees surface patterns. The specificity and hedging checks in `references/human-voice-en.md` still have to be done by reading. If Python is unavailable, perform the same checklist manually and keep writing.
6. Return the polished text. If you made structural changes (merged paragraphs, reordered sentences), say so in one line at the end. Do not produce a long change-log unless asked.

### When the user asks for a logic or rigor review

1. Read `references/logic-check.md`.
2. Identify the manuscript section, study design, research question, primary outcomes, and available evidence.
3. Check the chain from rationale and objective through methods, results, interpretation, and conclusion.
4. Report major, moderate, and minor logic issues before rewriting. Distinguish confirmed errors from likely problems and missing information.
5. Rewrite only after the audit unless the user explicitly asks for a direct rewrite.
6. After the reasoning is sound, apply the relevant language, genre, field, and AI-trace guidance.

### When the user gives you data to analyze and write up

1. Inspect the data file (Excel / CSV). Confirm with the user: what is the design (between-subjects, within-subjects, mixed)? What are the dependent variables? What comparison do they want?
2. Run `python scripts/stats.py` or `py scripts/stats.py` with the appropriate test when the required packages are installed. The script outputs descriptives, the test result, effect size, and a Results-section paragraph in the requested language.
3. Review the auto-generated paragraph. Tighten it, strip any AI traces, adjust hedging to match the field's convention.
4. If a figure is needed, use `scripts/nature_plot.py` (see "Figures" below).

### When the user asks for a figure

1. Confirm: which variables, which comparison, what figure type (bar with error bars, box+jitter, scatter+regression, line with shaded CI, forest plot for meta-analysis).
2. Use `python scripts/nature_plot.py` or `py scripts/nature_plot.py` from the skill directory when the required packages are installed. It loads `assets/matplotlibrc` automatically, which enforces Nature-style defaults: Helvetica/Arial, 7-8pt, no gridlines, outward ticks, left+bottom spines only, colorblind-safe palette, 300 DPI.
3. Always show individual data points overlaid on summary statistics for n ≤ 30 (box+jitter or violin+strip). Sport science samples are usually small enough that individual variability matters.
4. Mark significance with explicit p-values where space allows. Use `*` `**` `***` only when there are many comparisons. Always state in the caption what the asterisks mean and what the error bars represent (SD, SEM, or 95% CI). Vague error bars are a reviewer red flag.
5. Export to both PDF (vector, for submission) and PNG at 300 DPI (for preview). See `references/nature-figures.md` for the full spec.

### When the user asks for a translation (zh ↔ en)

Translate by rewriting in the target language's natural scientific register. Word-for-word mapping produces both translationese and AI tone. After translating:
- pass the output through the zero-tolerance list and the target-language AI-trace checklist. For zh→en, also run the positive check in `references/human-voice-en.md` §10
- check that hedging strength is preserved. Chinese tends to under-hedge and English tends to over-hedge, so calibrate
- check that citation format matches the target genre: 国标 for Chinese, APA7/Vancouver for English (see `references/citations.md`)

## Citation formats

- **English journals (most sport science)**: APA 7 (author-date) or Vancouver (numbered). Default to APA 7 unless the target journal is medical (then Vancouver). Full rules and examples in `references/citations.md`.
- **Chinese journals and theses**: GB/T 7714-2015. Format is strict. See `references/citations.md`.

Do not invent DOIs or fill in missing fields. If the user's reference is incomplete, flag it and ask.

## Statistics

The most common tests in sport science and how to report them are in `references/sport-stats.md`. The `scripts/stats.py` helper covers:

- descriptives (mean, SD, median, IQR, 95% CI)
- independent and paired t-tests with Cohen's d / Hedges' g
- one-way and repeated-measures ANOVA with η²p
- Pearson and Spearman correlation
- reliability (ICC, Cronbach's α)
- normality checks (Shapiro-Wilk) and non-parametric alternatives

For mixed-effects models, meta-analysis, or other advanced methods, use Python (`statsmodels`, `pingouin`) or R directly and write the script ad hoc. Still report results following the conventions in `references/sport-stats.md`.

- 正文分号 / semicolons outside brackets

# sportsci-workflow

**One repository for the whole sport-science writing workflow: choose a topic, analyse the data and make the figures, polish the prose, and keep the citations alive in Word.**

[中文说明](README.zh-CN.md)

![One workflow, four skills](assets/workflow_en.png)

Four small skills that each do one job, hand files to the next, and can also be used alone. Each is both an
[agent skill](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills) (a `SKILL.md` that tells an AI agent how to work) and a command-line tool.

| # | Skill | Question it answers | Main output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [`sportsci-topic`](skills/sportsci-topic) | Is this topic crowded, possible and affordable? Which design, how many people? | topic card + `design.json` draft |
| 2 | [`sportsci-figures`](skills/sportsci-figures) | What do the data say, and how is it shown? | figures (zh / en), three-line tables, Results `.docx`, methods explained |
| 3 | [`sportsci-writing`](skills/sportsci-writing) | Does the prose read like a person wrote it, and is the logic sound? | revised text, checker report |
| 4 | [`sportsci-refs`](skills/sportsci-refs) | Are the citations real, consistent and still editable? | `.docx` with live Zotero fields, verification report |

## What they have in common

- **No invention.** Data, references, effect sizes and gaps come from files you supply or from computation; when something is missing the tool says so.
- **Rules you can read.** Thresholds and checks are written next to their verdicts (`sportsci-topic`), numbers in text come from the analysis objects (`sportsci-figures`), edits never touch Zotero fields (`sportsci-refs`).
- **Chinese and English.** Figures, tables, cards and guidance exist in both sets; a deliverable never mixes them.
- **New files, not overwrites.** Each command writes a new file and verifies it.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gaibin/sportsci-workflow.git
```

## A pass through the workflow

```bash
# 1  topic: a brief, your exported records, one card
sportsci-topic new -o brief.toml
sportsci-topic card brief.toml -r cnki.csv -r pubmed.ris -o topic_out --lang zh
sportsci-figures check-design topic_out/design_draft.json -d data.csv

# 2  data: analysis, figures, tables, Results document

# 3  writing: polish the draft with the agent; the trace checker flags formulaic patterns
```

## Colour rule

All figures use one navy palette. The one deliberate exception is the eye-tracking fixation heat map, which uses the rainbow-type `turbo`
map because that is the field's convention; it is a default of that block only and can be overridden with `cmap=`.

## Scope and limits

- The tools check, count, compute and format. They do not decide what is important, and they do not replace a supervisor or an ethics committee.
- `sportsci-writing` does not promise to pass any AI-detection score; it removes formulaic patterns and asks for the specifics only the author has.
- A DOI check shows a paper exists with matching metadata, not that it supports the sentence it is cited for.
- Windows and Word with Zotero 7 are the tested environment for `sportsci-refs`; the document editing itself is plain OOXML.

# sportsci-figures

**Publication-grade figures, three-line tables and a ready-to-edit Results section for sport, exercise and health science — from one
design file and your data, in Chinese or English.**

[中文说明](README.zh-CN.md)

![Figures produced by sportsci-figures](assets/hero.png)

- **Six study designs run end to end**: RCT pre–post (ANCOVA), crossover and multi-timepoint (mixed models), single-group repeated
  measures, questionnaire surveys (reliability, EFA, regression, bootstrap mediation, moderation) and meta-analysis.
- **One command → a full Results package**: figures (300-dpi PNG + vector PDF), three-line tables (Word + Excel), the Results text, and a
  methods explanation that justifies every analytic choice with the study's own numbers.
- **26 more data types** as reusable figure blocks: CGM, EMG, force–time, SPM waveforms, GRF, IMU, survival, ROC, omics, GPS tracking …
- **Two language sets, one style**: every label, caption and table in all-Chinese or all-English; layout, colours and statistics identical.
- **Integrity built in**: every number comes from code, wording ("differed" / "did not differ") follows the multiplicity-adjusted P,
  simulated data are stamped on every figure.

## Designs

| Study | `design` | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| Parallel groups, baseline + follow-up | `parallel_prepost` | ANCOVA with baseline covariate, change scores, Hedges g, estimation plot, baseline table with SMD |
| Every participant in every condition | `crossover` | Random-intercept mixed model, marginal means, Holm-adjusted contrasts, dose–response trend, d_z |
| Parallel groups, ≥ 3 visits | `multitime` | Constrained longitudinal mixed model, CI ribbons, supplementary group × time ANOVA (Greenhouse–Geisser) |
| One group, 2+ visits | `single_group` | Paired t + Wilcoxon or repeated-measures ANOVA (Mauchly, Greenhouse–Geisser, Bonferroni) |
| Questionnaire | `survey` | Cronbach α, KMO/Bartlett, EFA, common-method bias, correlations, group differences, regression, bootstrap mediation, moderation |
| Evidence synthesis | `meta` | Random effects (DerSimonian–Laird + Hartung–Knapp), subgroups, leave-one-out, Egger, meta-regression |

Primary outcomes are Holm-adjusted, secondary outcomes Benjamini–Hochberg within category. Field reference: [`reference/DESIGN_SPEC.md`](reference/DESIGN_SPEC.md).

# sportsci-refs

**Turn the typed `[12]` citations in a Word thesis into live Zotero fields — then edit, renumber and verify the document without ever breaking them.**

[中文说明](README.zh-CN.md)

![From a draft with typed [n] to citations Zotero can refresh](assets/pipeline_en.png)

Most reference tooling stops at "export a list". The hard part comes after: the Word file already has fields, you must change a sentence,
move a citation, or fix the numbering — and one careless "select the paragraph and retype it" silently destroys every citation in it.
`sportsci-refs` treats the Word citation field as the unit it is, and checks the result with machine tests instead of "looks fine".

- **Search and verify.** Candidate literature from Crossref, Europe PMC and OpenAlex (peer-review records stripped, de-duplicated),
  every DOI resolved on Crossref with a title comparison — a *real* DOI attached to the *wrong* paper is reported as `MISMATCH`.
- **Typed list → Zotero.** Parse a hand-typed GB/T 7714 reference list into RIS / CSL-JSON, import, and match it to a Zotero collection by DOI, then title.
- **`[n]` → live Zotero fields.** Plain-text citations become real `ADDIN ZOTERO_ITEM` fields and the list becomes one bibliography field.
- **Field-safe editing.** Replace text, move a citation in front of the full stop, renumber by first appearance — only plain text outside fields
  changes; the bibliography is recognised as "inside a field" even though its markers sit in other paragraphs.
- **13 machine checks** (`verify`): balanced markers, payload JSON, display = payload, numbering = order of first appearance,
  citation before punctuation, bibliography numbering / tabs / title match, cited-but-not-listed, listed-but-not-cited.
- **GB/T 7714-2015** numeric list generation when Zotero is not used; Chinese and English entries.

## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gaibin/sportsci-workflow.git
cd sportsci-workflow/skills/sportsci-refs
pip install -e .

sportsci-refs status                                    # Zotero reachable? (needs Zotero 7 running)
sportsci-refs parse refs.txt -o refs                    # typed GB/T 7714 list -> refs.ris + refs.json
sportsci-refs check-doi refs.ris -o doi.md              # OK / EXISTS / MISMATCH / 404 / NODOI
#   Zotero: select a new collection, File -> Import -> refs.ris
sportsci-refs match refs.txt -c "My thesis" -o zotero_match.json
sportsci-refs fieldify thesis.docx -m zotero_match.json --superscript -o thesis_Zotero.docx
#   Word: Zotero -> Document Preferences -> choose the style -> Refresh
sportsci-refs verify thesis_Zotero.docx -o report.md    # every count must be 0
```

Edit later, safely:

```bash
sportsci-refs edit thesis_Zotero.docx -r "下降趋势=>降低趋势" -r "decline=>decrease" -o v2.docx
sportsci-refs renumber v2.docx -o v3.docx               # then Word -> Zotero -> Refresh for the bibliography
sportsci-refs compare thesis_Zotero.docx v3.docx        # only word/document.xml may differ
```

```python
from sportsci_refs.fieldedit import FieldDoc, detach

doc = FieldDoc("thesis_Zotero.docx")
doc.replace("下降趋势", "降低趋势")                         # plain text only
_, group = doc.citations()[0]
ok, msg = doc.insert_before_anchor(paragraph_index, "。", detach(group))   # refuses ambiguous anchors
doc.refresh_numbers()
doc.save("v2.docx")        # refuses to overwrite the source, refuses to write a document whose field counts changed
```

Settings (Zotero user ID, data folder, contact e-mail) live in `config/local.toml` (copy `config/local.example.toml`; git-ignored) or environment variables.

## Why it is built this way

| What goes wrong | Consequence | What this tool does |
|---|---|---|
| A paragraph is rewritten as "delete all runs, append one" | Citations vanish silently — a 70-run paragraph typically has only 25 plain-text runs | Only runs outside fields are edited |
| `document.xml` is round-tripped through a parser that hoists inline namespace declarations | Word: "the file is corrupt" (pictures declare `xmlns:a` inline) | String splice or lxml; every other package part copied byte for byte |
| The bibliography is treated as ordinary text | Edits are overwritten at the next Refresh | Field depth is tracked across the whole document |
| The anchor text occurs twice | The citation lands in the wrong sentence, no error | Anchors must be unique, otherwise the edit is refused |
| A checker says "37 inconsistencies" | You fix 37 non-problems (en dash vs hyphen, split `instrText`, RTF-encoded dashes) | Those false alarms are normalised before comparing |
| `HTTP 502` from `127.0.0.1:23119` | Looks like a broken Zotero; actually a local proxy answering because Zotero is not running | Local calls bypass proxies, external APIs use them; `status` explains it |

Full playbook (Chinese, with Word COM checks and framed-template notes): [`reference/ZOTERO_PLAYBOOK.md`](reference/ZOTERO_PLAYBOOK.md).

`SKILL.md` gives an agent the pipeline, the iron rules and the checks. Clone into your skills folder:

# sportsci-refs

**把 Word 论文里手打的 `[12]` 变成 Zotero 能自动刷新的引文域——之后改稿、重新编号、校验，都不会把它弄坏。**

[English](README.md)

![从手打 [n] 的草稿，到 Zotero 能自动刷新的引文](assets/pipeline_zh.png)

大多数文献工具只做到"导出一个列表"。真正麻烦的是之后：Word 里已经有引文域，你要改一句话、挪一个引文、修编号——
一次"选中整段重打"，就会悄无声息地把这一段里的所有引文毁掉。`sportsci-refs` 把 Word 的引文域当成它本来的样子来处理，
并且用机器检查来验收，而不是"看着没问题"。

- **检索与核验**：从 Crossref、Europe PMC、OpenAlex 检索候选（剔除同行评审记录、按 DOI 去重）；每个 DOI 在 Crossref 上解析并比对题名——
  "真实存在的 DOI 挂在错误的论文上"会被报为 `MISMATCH`。
- **手打列表 → Zotero**：把手打的 GB/T 7714 文献表解析成 RIS / CSL-JSON，导入后按 DOI、再按题名匹配到 Zotero 分类。
- **`[n]` → Zotero 引文域**：纯文本引用变成真正的 `ADDIN ZOTERO_ITEM` 域，文献表变成一个文献表域。
- **域安全改稿**：替换文字、把引文挪到句号前、按首次出现顺序重新编号——只有域外的普通文字会变；
  文献表即使起止标记在别的段落里，也会被识别为"在域内"。
- **13 项机检**（`verify`）：标记配对、载荷 JSON、显示与载荷一致、编号 = 首次出现顺序、引文在标点前、文献表编号/制表符/题名对应、引而未列、列而未引。
- **GB/T 7714-2015** 顺序编码制文献表生成（不用 Zotero 时），中英文条目均可。

## 快速开始

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gaibin/sportsci-workflow.git
cd sportsci-workflow/skills/sportsci-refs
pip install -e .

sportsci-refs status                                    # Zotero 是否可达（需要 Zotero 7 正在运行）
sportsci-refs parse 文献表.txt -o 文献表                # 手打的 GB/T 7714 列表 -> 文献表.ris + 文献表.json
sportsci-refs check-doi 文献表.ris -o doi核验.md        # OK / EXISTS / MISMATCH / 404 / NODOI
#   Zotero：新建分类并选中 → 文件 → 导入 → 文献表.ris
sportsci-refs match 文献表.txt -c "我的论文" -o zotero_match.json
sportsci-refs fieldify 论文.docx -m zotero_match.json --superscript -o 论文_Zotero.docx
#   Word：Zotero → Document Preferences → 选学校要求的样式 → Refresh
sportsci-refs verify 论文_Zotero.docx -o 校验报告.md    # 每一项必须为 0
```

之后改稿：

```bash
sportsci-refs edit 论文_Zotero.docx -r "下降趋势=>降低趋势" -o v2.docx
sportsci-refs renumber v2.docx -o v3.docx               # 再到 Word 里点 Zotero → Refresh 重排文献表
sportsci-refs compare 论文_Zotero.docx v3.docx          # 只有 word/document.xml 应该变化
```

本机设置（Zotero 用户 ID、数据目录、联系邮箱）写在 `config/local.toml`（复制 `config/local.example.toml`，已被 git 忽略）或环境变量里。

## 为什么这样做

| 常见错误 | 后果 | 本工具的做法 |
|---|---|---|
| 把一个段落"删掉所有 run、再追加一个" | 引文无声消失；一段 70 个 run 里往往只有 25 个是普通文字 | 只改域外的 run |
| 用会提升内联命名空间的方式读写 `document.xml` | Word 报"文件已损坏"（图片在段内声明 `xmlns:a`） | 字符串拼接或 lxml，其余部件逐字节复制 |
| 把文献表当普通文字 | 改动在下次 Refresh 时被整体覆盖 | 全文档跟踪域的嵌套深度 |
| 锚点文字出现两次 | 引文插到错误的句子，且不报错 | 锚点必须唯一，否则拒绝 |
| 校验脚本报"37 处不一致" | 你去修 37 个并不存在的问题（en dash / 连字符、`instrText` 被拆分、RTF 编码的破折号） | 比较前先归一化这些误报 |
| 访问 `127.0.0.1:23119` 返回 502 | 看起来像 Zotero 坏了，实际是本机代理在应答——Zotero 没开 | 本地接口绕过代理，外网接口走代理；`status` 会解释 |

# sportsci-topic

**Choose a sport-science topic with evidence, a design, a sample size and a feasibility check — every number computed, every rule printed.**

[中文说明](README.zh-CN.md)

![From a vague interest to a topic you can defend](assets/pipeline_en.png)

"Is this topic doable?" is usually answered by feel. `sportsci-topic` answers it with four questions that can be counted:

1. **Is it crowded?** — your own record set (CNKI / PubMed / Zotero exports) is matched against the population, intervention and outcome of the question; you get overlap counts, the nearest studies, and statements such as *"14 records cover this population and intervention, none measures this outcome"*.
2. **Which design answers it, and what may you claim?** — an explicit rule table, not a suggestion.
3. **Are there enough people?** — exact power at the number you can really recruit, and the *smallest effect that number can detect*.
4. **Do you have the weeks, the instruments, the ethics route and the statistics?** — green / yellow / red, with the rule printed next to each.

The result is a one-page **topic card** (Chinese or English) and a `design.json` draft that [`sportsci-figures`](../sportsci-figures) can validate and analyse.

What it deliberately does not do: invent references, score hypotheses with a model, write a research gap for you, or add up a "quality score".
A gap is only ever stated about *your record set*, with the counts it rests on.

## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gaibin/sportsci-workflow.git
cd sportsci-workflow/skills/sportsci-topic
pip install -e .

sportsci-topic new -o brief.toml        # a commented form: question terms (zh + en), outcomes, constraints, effect source
sportsci-topic check brief.toml         # errors, warnings, the design it maps to, the queries it would run
sportsci-topic card brief.toml -r cnki.csv -r pubmed.ris -o topic_out --lang en
#   topic_out/topic_card.md      the card
#   topic_out/design_draft.json  -> sportsci-figures check-design
#   topic_out/topic_data.json    every number on the card
```

Try it without any data of your own: `python cli.py card examples/demo_brief.toml -r examples/demo_records.csv -o demo --this-year 2025`
(the demo records are synthetic and labelled as such).

### What the card looks like

```
🔴 red items: change the topic or the constraints first
 🔴 Sample size   d = 0.70: needs 68 analysed (80 enrolled with dropout); 40 accessible, about 34 analysed, power 0.51;
                  that n detects d ≈ 0.99 at 80% power.
 🟢 Time          needs 22 weeks (ethics 4 + recruitment 2 + intervention 8 + testing 2 + analysis/writing 6); 28 available; slack 6.
 🟡 Ethics        ethics pending: no recruitment or data collection before approval
 🟢 Overlap       30 records; direct overlap in the last 5 years: 1 (2 in all years).
```

The red row is the useful one: with 40 people the study can only detect an effect of about d = 1.0. The options are a stronger
or longer intervention, a within-subject design, a more responsive outcome, or more people — the card lists them, you decide.

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `new` | writes a commented `brief.toml` (refuses to overwrite) |
| `check` | validates the brief and shows the design and search queries |
| `evidence` | overlap counts by P / I / O combination, nearest studies, record-set statements |
| `variants` | changes one axis at a time (population, intervention, comparator, outcome) and recounts |
| `power` | `two-sample`, `paired`, `ancova`, `correlation`, `anova`, `regression`: required n, or power and smallest detectable effect for a given n |
| `card` | all of the above → card, design draft, data file; `--fetch` searches through `sportsci-refs` when it is installed |

```bash
sportsci-topic power two-sample -e 0.5 --dropout 0.15      # d = 0.500: n1 = 64 ... enrol 76 per arm
sportsci-topic power two-sample --n 17                     # n = 17 per group: smallest detectable d = 0.99
sportsci-topic power ancova --delta 3 --sd 5 --r-prepost 0.6
```

```python
from sportsci_topic.pipeline import run
r = run("brief.toml", ["cnki.csv"], lang="en")
r.assessment["overall"], r.evidence.direct_recent, r.plan.mdes_at_accessible
```

## Records

Export from CNKI / Wanfang / Web of Science / PubMed / Zotero. Accepted: `.csv` (UTF-8 or GBK; headers such as `Title-题名`, `Year-年`, `Summary-摘要` are recognised),
`.ris`, `.json` (CSL-JSON or a list of `{title, year, …}`) and `.txt` (one title or one GB/T 7714 entry per line).
With [`sportsci-refs`](../sportsci-refs) installed, `--fetch` runs pairwise queries (P+I, I+O, P+O, P+I+O) in both languages.

## Why it is built this way

| Common failure | Consequence | What this does |
|---|---|---|
| Canned "consensus and controversies" text | the same paragraph for every topic; looks like a literature review, is not | no text about the literature is generated — only counts |
| Ranking ideas by word overlap with the input | numbers that look precise and mean nothing | no score; each check has its own rule and colour |
| Sample size from a template or a rule of "30 per group" | the study cannot detect the effect it was designed for | exact power; reports the smallest detectable effect at the n you can recruit |
| An empty search result read as "nobody has done this" | a crowded topic is chosen | a variant with no matching record is "not assessable"; fewer than 30 records is flagged as a sketch |
| Effect size picked to make n small | an unfundable, unpublishable plan | the effect size must name its source or the sample size is marked illustrative |
| The same suggested topic for every student | duplicate theses | variants are counted against the student's own records, one axis at a time |

Every threshold and rule: [`reference/METHOD.md`](reference/METHOD.md). Every brief field: [`reference/BRIEF_FIELDS.md`](reference/BRIEF_FIELDS.md).

## Use it as an AI agent skill

`SKILL.md` splits the work: the agent builds the bilingual search vocabulary, proposes variants and explains the card; the code counts and calculates.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gaibin/sportsci-workflow.git
cp -r sportsci-workflow/skills/sportsci-topic ~/.claude/skills/
pip install -e ~/.claude/skills/sportsci-topic
```

## Scope and limits

- It says whether a topic is crowded, possible and affordable. It cannot say whether it is important or interesting.
- It does not read papers: a record that mentions all three facets may still study something else. Read the nearest studies.
- CNKI cannot be searched automatically; export the records.
- Multi-time-point mixed models have no closed-form power; ANCOVA at the final time point is used and labelled.
- Survey sample sizes are rules of thumb unless you supply `r` or `f²`.

Part of [sportsci-workflow](../../README.md): **sportsci-topic** (this module) → **sportsci-figures** → **sportsci-writing** → **sportsci-refs**.

# sportsci-topic

**用证据、设计、样本量和可行性检查来选运动科学的题——每个数字都是算出来的，每条规则都摆在明面上。**

[English](README.md)

![从一个模糊的兴趣，到一个能答辩的选题](assets/pipeline_zh.png)

"这个题能不能做？"通常靠感觉回答。`sportsci-topic` 把它拆成四个可以数出来的问题：

1. **撞题吗？** 把你自己导出的题录（CNKI / PubMed / Zotero）按问题里的人群、干预、结局去匹配，得到重叠计数、最接近的研究，
   以及这样的陈述：*"记录集中有 14 条同时涉及该人群与干预，没有一条测了这个结局"*。
2. **用什么设计，能下什么结论？** 一张明确的规则表，而不是"建议"。
3. **人够不够？** 按你实际能招到的人数算精确功效，并给出**这个人数能检出的最小效应**。
4. **周数、设备、伦理流程、统计基础够不够？** 绿 / 黄 / 红，规则就印在每一项旁边。

产出是一页**选题卡**（中文或英文）和一份 [`sportsci-figures`](../sportsci-figures) 能直接校验和分析的 `design.json` 草稿。

它有意**不做**的事：编造文献、用模型给假设打分、替你写研究缺口、把各项加成一个"质量分"。
缺口只会被陈述为"你这份记录集里的事实"，并带上它依据的计数。

## 快速开始

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gaibin/sportsci-workflow.git
cd sportsci-workflow/skills/sportsci-topic
pip install -e .

sportsci-topic new -o brief.toml        # 带注释的表单：问题的中英文检索词、测量指标、现实约束、效应量来源
sportsci-topic check brief.toml         # 报错、警告、对应的设计、将要用的检索式
sportsci-topic card brief.toml -r cnki.csv -r pubmed.ris -o topic_out --lang zh
#   topic_out/topic_card.md      选题卡
#   topic_out/design_draft.json  -> sportsci-figures check-design
#   topic_out/topic_data.json    卡片上每个数字的来源
```

没有自己的数据也能试：`python cli.py card examples/demo_brief.toml -r examples/demo_records.csv -o demo --this-year 2025`
（示例题录是合成的，并且都标注了"synthetic example"）。

### 卡片长什么样

```
🔴 有红色项：调整选题或条件后再继续
 🔴 样本量  d = 0.70：需要分析 68 人（含脱落约入组 80）；可及 40 人，脱落后约 34，功效 0.51；
            该人数能以 80% 功效检出的最小效应 d ≈ 0.99。
 🟢 时间    需要 22 周（伦理 4 + 招募 2 + 干预 8 + 测试 2 + 分析写作 6），可用 28 周，余量 6 周。
 🟡 伦理    伦理审批中：批准前不能招募或收集数据
 🟢 撞题    30 条记录；近 5 年直接重叠 1 条（全部年份 2 条）。
```

红色这一行最有用：40 个人只能检出约 d = 1.0 的效应。出路是更强或更长的干预、受试者自身对照的设计、更敏感的指标，
或者更多的人——卡片把选项列出来，由你决定。

## 命令

| 命令 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `new` | 生成带注释的 `brief.toml`（不覆盖已有文件） |
| `check` | 校验简报，显示对应设计与检索式 |
| `evidence` | 按 P / I / O 组合统计重叠，列出最接近的研究和记录集陈述 |
| `variants` | 每次改一个轴（人群、干预、对照、结局）并重新统计 |
| `power` | `two-sample`、`paired`、`ancova`、`correlation`、`anova`、`regression`：算所需人数，或给定人数时算功效与最小可检出效应 |
| `card` | 以上全部 → 选题卡、设计草稿、数据文件；装了 `sportsci-refs` 时可用 `--fetch` 联网检索 |

```bash
sportsci-topic power two-sample -e 0.5 --dropout 0.15      # d = 0.500：每组 64，含脱落入组 76
sportsci-topic power two-sample --n 17                     # 每组 17 人：最小可检出 d = 0.99
sportsci-topic power ancova --delta 3 --sd 5 --r-prepost 0.6
```

```python
from sportsci_topic.pipeline import run
r = run("brief.toml", ["cnki.csv"], lang="zh")
r.assessment["overall"], r.evidence.direct_recent, r.plan.mdes_at_accessible
```

## 题录

从 CNKI / 万方 / Web of Science / PubMed / Zotero 导出。支持 `.csv`（UTF-8 或 GBK；能识别 `Title-题名`、`Year-年`、`Summary-摘要` 这类表头）、
`.ris`、`.json`（CSL-JSON 或 `{title, year, …}` 列表）和 `.txt`（每行一个题名或一条 GB/T 7714 文献）。
装了 [`sportsci-refs`](../sportsci-refs) 后，`--fetch` 会用两两组合（P+I、I+O、P+O、P+I+O）的中英文检索式去查。

## 为什么这样做

| 常见错误 | 后果 | 本工具的做法 |
|---|---|---|
| 写死的"研究共识与争议" | 任何题目都是同一段话，像文献综述但不是 | 不生成任何关于文献的文字，只给计数 |
| 用与输入的词重合度给想法排名 | 数字看起来精确，其实没有信息 | 没有综合分；每项有自己的规则和颜色 |
| 样本量照搬模板或"每组 30 人" | 研究检不出它设计时想检的效应 | 精确功效；给出你能招到的人数下的最小可检出效应 |
| 把"没检索到"当成"没人做过" | 选了一个很拥挤的题 | 变体的检索词在记录集里一条都没有，就标"不可判断"；不足 30 条标为草图 |
| 为了让 n 小而挑效应量 | 做不下去也发不出去的方案 | 效应量必须写来源，否则样本量只作示意 |
| 同一个建议选题给所有学生 | 论文撞题 | 变体在你自己的记录集里逐轴统计 |

所有阈值与规则：[`reference/METHOD.md`](reference/METHOD.md)；简报每个字段：[`reference/BRIEF_FIELDS.md`](reference/BRIEF_FIELDS.md)。

## 作为 AI 技能使用

`SKILL.md` 把工作分开：智能体负责整理中英文检索词、提出变体并解读卡片；计数和计算都交给代码。

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gaibin/sportsci-workflow.git
cp -r sportsci-workflow/skills/sportsci-topic ~/.claude/skills/
pip install -e ~/.claude/skills/sportsci-topic
```

## 适用范围与限制

- 它说明一个题是否拥挤、能否做成、做不做得起；它不能说明题目是否重要、有没有意思。
- 它不读论文：摘要里同时出现三个要素的记录，研究的可能是别的东西。要读最接近的研究。
- CNKI 不能自动检索，请自己导出题录。
- 多时间点混合模型没有闭式功效公式，这里用终测时点的 ANCOVA 并标注。
- 问卷研究的样本量是经验规则，除非你提供 `r` 或 `f²`。

# sportsci-writing

A portable agent skill for writing, polishing, and translating sport science manuscripts (journal papers, theses, reviews) in Chinese and English, with built-in statistics and Nature-style figure generation.

Designed to work with **any agent CLI** that can read a markdown instruction file and execute Python:

- Claude Code
- OpenAI Codex CLI
- Cursor / Cline / Continue
- Aider
- Custom agents built on the Anthropic / OpenAI SDKs

## What it does

- Polishes Chinese or English sport science prose so it does **not** read like AI output (strips em-dashes used as asides, mechanical "首先/其次", "delve/leverage/crucial", overused parentheses, name-and-restate paragraph shapes, etc.)
- Drafts and restructures sections of empirical papers (IMRaD), narrative/systematic reviews, and BS/MS/PhD theses
- Translates between Chinese and English in the natural register of the target language, not word-for-word
- Audits research logic from the research question through methods, results, discussion, and conclusion
- Runs descriptive and inferential statistics (t-test, ANOVA, correlation, effect sizes, reliability) and writes the Results paragraph for you
- Produces Nature-quality figures (box+jitter, violin+strip, bar+error, scatter+regression, forest plot) with sane defaults
- Formats references in APA 7, Vancouver, or GB/T 7714 (国标)

It will **not** fabricate data, citations, p-values, or DOIs. If something is missing it asks.

## Install

Drop the `sportsci-writing/` directory anywhere your agent can read it.

### Claude Code

```bash
# project-scoped
mv sportsci-writing .claude/skills/

# or user-scoped (all projects)
mv sportsci-writing ~/.claude/skills/
```

Claude Code auto-discovers `SKILL.md` files in those locations.

### Codex / Cursor / other agents

Point your agent at `sportsci-writing/SKILL.md` as system context, or symlink it into whatever instruction directory the tool uses (`.cursor/rules/`, `AGENTS.md` include, etc.). The skill is plain markdown plus Python, with no Claude-specific APIs.

### Python dependencies (for scripts/)

```bash
pip install pandas numpy scipy statsmodels pingouin matplotlib openpyxl
```

## Usage

Just talk to the agent. Examples:

- "帮我把这段方法部分润色一下" → polish + AI-trace scrub
- "Translate the discussion to English, target journal is *MSSE*" → translate + journal-style adjustments
- "Run a paired t-test on `pre_post.xlsx` (column A = pre, B = post) and write the Results paragraph in Chinese" → stats + auto-drafted paragraph
- "Make a Nature-style box plot comparing VO2max across three training groups" → figure with proper defaults
- "这篇综述的引言读起来太 AI 了，重写" → full rewrite, stripping AI tells

## No agent? Use the prompt

Paste `prompts/精简版提示词.txt` (or `prompts/quick-prompt-en.txt`) at the start of a chat with any assistant, then add your text. It carries the
core rules: invent nothing, remove AI-sounding prose, drop defensive tone while keeping primary outcomes, null results and limitations, and
change as little as possible.

## Tests

The trace checker is tested against the human rewrites in `references/before-after.md` and, when you keep a local `references/voice-samples/` folder, the journal paragraphs in it: none of them may produce a hit. The author's personal rules (dashes, semicolons, contrast frames) are excluded from that check because published prose uses them routinely. They have their own test cases. Run after changing any rule:

```bash
python -m unittest discover tests -v
```

No extra dependencies. pytest also works if installed.

### 2.4 Study notes

These notes restate the course's main editing rules in new sentences. The examples were written for this repository. They are not lines from the lectures or from the article. The substitutions in unit 1 and unit 2 are the ones the article says the course repeats; the same pairs are listed again, with sources, in [`clutter-words.md`](clutter-words.md).

**Unit 1. Delete words that do not change the claim.**

Read the sentence and mark every word that could go without changing who did what, to what, and with what result. Then delete those words.

Common cuts the article attributes to this unit:

| Longer wording | Shorter wording |
|---|---|
| in order to | to |
| due to the fact that | because |
| at the present time | now |
| has the potential to / has the ability to | can |
| a sufficient number of | enough |
| in spite of the fact that | although |

Also delete empty openers that add no finding: "It was observed that", "It is well known that". If the sentence still needs a hedge, use one verb of the right strength (see the writing skill's hedging table), not a stack of openers.

**Unit 2. Put the real action in the verb.**

A frequent pattern is a thin verb plus a noun that hides the action: "conduct an evaluation of", "perform a measurement of", "achieve an improvement in". The action is already in the noun. Use that word as the verb: evaluate, measure, improve. The subject and the verb then sit next to each other, and the chain of "of" / "by" gets shorter.

**Unit 2. Use the active voice when the actor is part of the claim.**

For work the author team did, "We measured" and "We found" name the actor and are usually shorter than "It was measured". Module 2 has a separate video on "we" and "I". Passive remains useful when the actor is not the point. The usual case in a paper is a method step in which the procedure matters more than which person ran it. Section 4 records how Nature's current page, Nature's Masterclasses post, and this repository's own Methods note say the same thing. Check the target journal before making every sentence active.

**Units 3 and 4, in one pass.** One sentence should carry one claim, plus the conditions that belong with that claim. Do not shorten a sentence by deleting the instrument, the time point, or the estimate. Do shorten it by deleting the empty words from unit 1. Paragraphs need a point in the first sentence. Revision is a separate step from the first draft. The page's module 4 says this directly.

**Unit 5. What each part of an original paper has to do.** The article's summary of this unit, restated:

- Introduction. Move from what the field already accepts, to the gap or the conflicting findings, to this paper's question. The introduction's job is to leave the reader with that unanswered question. A list of papers is not yet an introduction.
- Methods. Another lab should be able to repeat the work. Split the section by time or by experiment. Do not discuss, and do not put results in Methods.
- Results. Write the finding, then the estimate (effect, difference, or P) in parentheses, then the figure or table number. Do not read the table out as a second table.
- Discussion. Start by answering the question the introduction asked. Then compare with earlier studies and give a reason for agreement or disagreement. Then state the limits of this study. Then say what the result means beyond this sample.

Module 5 on Coursera also covers tables, figures, and the abstract, in the video order listed in §2.3. The article's unit 5 does not expand on those two.

**A worked pass on a sport-science sentence.** Original example, not a course excerpt:

> An evaluation of countermovement jump height was conducted using a force plate in order to achieve the determination of lower-limb power.

Three separate problems: the actions sit inside "evaluation" and "determination", the actor is missing, and "in order to" adds no meaning. One revision:

> We measured countermovement jump height on a force plate to determine lower-limb power.

Results, same rules:

> It was observed that there was an increase in session RPE after the congested fixture week.

> Session RPE increased after the congested fixture week.

Put the size of the increase, the comparison, and the figure number in the same sentence when you have them. Do not invent them to make the sentence look finished.

Discussion, same rules:

> The findings of the present study are indicative of the fact that the cooling vest has the ability to lower core temperature.

> The cooling vest lowered core temperature at the end of the trial (mean difference and 95% CI here; Figure N).

**Later units.** Modules 6–8 on the current page cover authorship, plagiarism, predatory journals, peer review, review articles, grants, letters, personal statements, and writing for the public. Use them when the task is one of those genres. A research-paper edit can stop after modules 1, 2, and 5 and still have the rules this repository uses most often.
